public_rationale: By publication, Sutskever and Hassabis had publicly described reduced gains from scaling, while Pichai had explained that further progress required breakthroughs beyond scaling alone. Marcus's March 2022 article explicitly raised possible diminishing returns. These records support the sentence under the ordinary reading of 'many' as several prominent figures. The result depends on that unquantified reading and on counting Pichai's qualified acknowledgment. It does not establish consensus, prove a technical scaling limit, or validate every part of Marcus's 2022 argument.
limitations: Pichai's acknowledgment is less explicit than those of Sutskever and Hassabis.
News reporting documents the statements; an accessible original transcript was not obtained for Sutskever.
The earlier Marcus article establishes prior wording only.
Prominent contemporaries remained optimistic about continued progress.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Many leading figures in the field have acknowledged that pure LLM scaling may have reached a period of diminishing returns, much as Marcus anticipated in 2022.
conditions: many leading figures in the field

statement.excerpt: Many leading figures in the field have acknowledged that we may have reached a period of diminishing returns of pure LLM scaling, much as I anticipated in 2022.
statement.document_title: Why I don’t share Sam Altman’s confidence that AGI is basically a solved problem

from_speaker: Many leading figures in the field have acknowledged
our_interpretation: This is a claim about public acknowledgments made by publication, not a forecast that scaling must cease to produce improvements.
Read 'pure LLM scaling' as increasing pretraining data, model size and compute without relying on distinct methodological advances or additional inference-time reasoning.
Read 'many leading figures' as several prominent researchers or leaders of major AI organizations, without implying a majority or consensus. Marcus supplies no numerical count.
The historical period begins in 2022 because the sentence explicitly includes his earlier warning and ends on the post date.
Marcus's 2022 writing can establish the existence and wording of his warning. It cannot establish that the warning was technically correct.
criteria.support_condition: Dated records show several prominent AI figures publicly acknowledging possible diminishing gains from pretraining scale alone before publication, and a 2022 record shows Marcus making a materially similar warning.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable records establish that the attributed acknowledgments occurred only after publication or materially misstate those figures' positions, or that the identified 2022 statement did not make the claimed warning.

evidence.excerpt: performance gains from bigger models have plateaued.
evidence.explanation: This contemporary report identifies Sutskever and explicitly describes his acknowledgment of a plateau. It is reputable secondary reporting of his position; the underlying Reuters interview was inaccessible through read_page.

evidence.excerpt: no longer getting the same progress.
evidence.locator: Hassabis interview passage following the discussion of scaling laws and available text
evidence.publisher: The New York Times, syndicated by The Indian Express
evidence.explanation: The report attributes this statement to Google DeepMind leader Demis Hassabis and explicitly describes his view that returns from adding training data were diminishing. It also preserves his qualification that existing techniques could still deliver improvements.

evidence.excerpt: it’s not just a question of scaling alone
evidence.locator: Interview answer beginning 'To be very clear about my answer'
evidence.explanation: In an original interview conducted Wednesday before publication, Google CEO Sundar Pichai explains that further progress requires breakthroughs beyond scaling alone. This supports the qualified reading of Marcus's sentence, although Pichai remained optimistic and did not declare that AI progress had stopped.

evidence.excerpt: perhaps already approaching a point of diminishing returns.
evidence.locator: Paragraph beginning 'Indeed, we may already', in the discussion of scaling laws
evidence.explanation: The dated article directly establishes that Marcus voiced a similar warning in 2022, in a discussion that includes GPT-3-like models. It is used only as a record of his statement, not as evidence that his technical assessment was right.

evidence.locator: Paragraph introducing the positions of Altman, Amodei and Huang
evidence.publisher: The New York Times, syndicated by The Indian Express
evidence.explanation: The report also identifies Sam Altman, Dario Amodei and Jensen Huang as optimistic about continued progress. This limits any reading of Marcus's statement as an industry consensus, but does not negate the existence of the cited acknowledgments.
